title: Immigration desk
setting: You've landed at Narita. You're at the front of the foreign passport queue.

n1.speaker: officer
n1.japanese: パスポートをお願いします。
n1.audioHint: パスポートをおねがいします

options.feedback: Hand it over open at the photo page. That's it.
どうぞ is the all-purpose 'here you go' when handing something over. Compact and natural.

n2.speaker: officer
n2.japanese: 旅行の目的は何ですか。
n2.romaji: Ryokō no mokuteki wa nan desu ka.
n2.english: What's the purpose of your visit?
n2.audioHint: りょこうのもくてきはなんですか

options.feedback: One word, exactly what's wanted. Immigration is not the place to be expansive.
Also correct, slightly fuller. Both land the same.
It'll be repeated in English and you'll be fine — but 目的 (purpose) is the one word worth knowing before you land.
Back on track, and answering in Japanese after a stumble reads well.

n3.speaker: officer
n3.english: How many days are you staying?
n3.audioHint: なんにちかんたいざいしますか

options.feedback: Ten days. Note 十日 is the irregular とおか, not じゅうにち.
週間 counts weeks. Often easier to say than the day count.
Best answer — show the booking on your phone as you say it. Place names are hard to pronounce and easy to show.
True but vague. Expect a follow-up asking which hotel, so have the address ready anyway.
'I understand' isn't an answer to 'where'. Under pressure it's easy to reach for a phrase you're confident in rather than the one that fits — worth noticing that reflex now.

n5.speaker: officer
n5.japanese: はい、結構です。指紋と写真をお願いします。
n5.romaji: Hai, kekkō desu. Shimon to shashin o onegai shimasu.
n5.english: That's fine. Fingerprints and photo, please.
n5.audioHint: はい、けっこうです。しもんとしゃしんをおねがいします

options.feedback: Now it fits — index fingers on the scanner, look at the small camera.
Also fine. 結構です here means 'that's sufficient', not 'no thank you' — context does the work.

end.speaker: narration
end.english: Stamped and through. Four questions, always the same four: purpose, length, where, and the biometrics.
